test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following steps is INCORRECT for micrometer adjustment?

options.text: Insert the large end of wrench in the hole on the external cylinder.
Find set screw and loosen it.
Use the wrench to rotate the cylinder until zero is aligned.
Open the micrometer using friction stop.

solution:
The correct answer is __Open the micrometer using friction stop**(Option 4)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Micrometer adjustment__ is a precise process used to ensure proper measurement accuracy.
 
• Steps such as loosening the set screw and rotating the cylinder to align zero are critical for calibration.
 
• Using the friction stop to open the micrometer is incorrect as it does not pertain to the calibration process.
 
• The friction stop is used to control the spindle movement during measurement, not for adjustment purposes.
 
• Correct adjustment involves tools like the provided wrench and careful alignment of the scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Micrometer:**

 
 
• A micrometer is a precision measuring instrument used for small dimensions.
 
• It typically measures dimensions in the range of 0.01 mm or 0.001 inches.
 
 
 
• **Friction Stop:**
 
 
• The friction stop helps prevent over-tightening of the spindle against the object being measured.
 
• It ensures consistent pressure during measurement, improving accuracy.
 
 
 
• **Wrench:**
 
 
• The wrench is a tool provided with the micrometer for calibration and adjustment purposes.
 
• It is used to rotate the cylinder or loosen screws during calibration.
